title: A.R. Rahman Becomes the Face of Brooke Bond Taj Mahal Tea
excerpt: Hindustan Unilever's tea brand, whose "Wah Taj!" line was made famous by Ustad Zakir Hussain, has signed the Oscar-winning composer for a new campaign about the creative pause.
body:
• Brooke Bond Taj Mahal Tea, owned by Hindustan Unilever, announced A.R. Rahman as its brand ambassador on November 2, launching a new platform called "Awaken Your Masterpiece."
  • In the campaign film, Rahman works through a creative block, pauses over a freshly brewed cup, and finds a melody — ending on the brand's signature "Wah Taj!" line.
  • The brand's music association runs back decades to tabla maestro Ustad Zakir Hussain, the earlier face of "Wah Taj!", who died in December 2024.
  • The campaign was conceptualised by Ogilvy India and the film was directed by Prakash Varma of Nirvana Films; it is live across the brand's digital and marketing platforms.

A.R. Rahman has a new stage: a cup of tea. Brooke Bond Taj Mahal Tea, the Hindustan Unilever brand built for over six decades around fine tea-making and the line "Hazaaron Mein Ek," announced the Oscar- and Grammy-winning composer as its brand ambassador on November 2, alongside a new campaign platform, "Awaken Your Masterpiece," Bollywood Hungama reported.

The film: a creative block, a pause, a melody

The campaign is built on a single idea — that a purposeful pause is part of making something good. In the film, Rahman is shown stuck in a creative block before turning to a freshly brewed cup of Taj Mahal Tea; the pause gives way to an uplifting melody, and the film closes with the brand's signature expression, "Wah Taj!" One version of the film then moves into the strains of "Tere Bina," Rahman's composition from the film Guru. The campaign film is now live across Taj Mahal Tea's digital and marketing platforms, according to Storyboard18.

A music lineage that predates Rahman

Taj Mahal Tea's link with music is not new packaging. The brand's "Wah Taj!" advertising was fronted for years by tabla maestro Ustad Zakir Hussain, who died in December 2024, afaqs! noted. Rahman's signing continues that association with a musician of a different instrument and generation, on the same argument the brand has always made: that blending tea and composing music are both crafts of patience and precision.

"Over decades, Taj Mahal Tea and music have been inseparable, a bond that began with the legendary Ustad Zakir Hussain and the iconic 'Wah Taj!'."

— Ishtpreet Singh, Vice President, Beverages, Hindustan Unilever

Who made the campaign

The campaign was conceptualised by Ogilvy India, led by Fritz Gonsalves and Jayesh Raut, with group chief creative officers Harshad Rajadhyaksha and Kainaz Karmakar. The film was shot by Prakash Varma of Nirvana Films, who has been part of the brand's visual language for over a decade. For Rahman, the signing adds a heritage Indian household brand to his public work in a year when his film music has kept him in the news; for the brand, it is a direct handover from one musical master to another.
